functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Part of a graded series with levator labii superioris alaeque nasi (medial) and zygomaticus minor (lateral), collectively deepening the nasolabial fold.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Over the nasolabial region lateral to the ala of the nose. In a 50-hemiface cadaveric study, the LLS insertion runs at a mean of 25.8 +/- 4.8 degrees from the facial midline and converges with levator labii superioris alaeque nasi (-20.2 +/- 3.2 degrees) and zygomaticus minor (55.7 +/- 6.4 degrees) at a common triangular area lateral to the ala, whose centroid was proposed as an injection point (the 'Yonsei point').
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: The insertion of LLS is partially or entirely covered by levator labii superioris alaeque nasi and zygomaticus minor; the three muscle vectors converge just lateral to the nasal ala rather than at a single discrete point, so BoNT placed at the shared centroid affects all three.
structures_at_risk: levator labii superioris alaeque nasi and zygomaticus minor, converging on the same target -- treatment here is inherently non-selective for LLS alone
infraorbital nerve branches, which run predominantly vertically through the upper lip/cheek in this region rather than horizontally
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: This landmark (not literally an ultrasound protocol, but a cadaveric surface-landmark method) was developed for gummy-smile treatment, where excessive gingival display from hyperactive lip elevators (LLS, LLSAN, zygomaticus minor) is reduced with low-dose BoNT-A at the convergence point; no side or sex differences in the muscle vector angles were found.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Hwang WS, Hur MS, Hu KS, Song WC, Koh KS, Baik HS, Kim ST, Kim HJ, Lee KJ, Angle Orthod 79(1):70-77 (2009), doi:10.2319/091407-437.1 (https://doi.org/10.2319/091407-437.1) -- retrieved via PubMed
